title: Homogeneous Watermark Blind Spots: Detector Monoculture Plus Output Homogeneity

original_idea.body:
# Homogeneous Watermark Blind Spots: Detector Monoculture Plus Output Homogeneity

**Problem:** Failure mode A: AI-text-detection / watermark fragility. Failure mode B: generator homogeneity. If all generators produce homogeneous text, a single paraphrase or style transform that evades one detector evades all of them — detection robustness collapses correlatedly across the fleet.

**Direction:** Generate text from 5-6 open models, run an open AI-text detector, then apply a fixed set of light transforms (paraphrase, register shift). Measure whether evasion transfers across generators and whether generator output-homogeneity predicts shared evasion. Report correlated-evasion rates vs an independence baseline.

**Why it matters:** AI-content governance (EU AI Act) leans on detection. Homogeneity means one evasion recipe defeats detection everywhere — a correlated governance failure. Cheap, fully external to labs.

**Relevant context:** Artificial Hivemind homogeneity; AI-text detection robustness literature; EU AI Act systemic-risk / transparency requirements.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible governance-failure chain, but AI-text detection is a diffuse misuse/transparency concern rather than a critical catastrophic-risk pathway.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Generation, an open detector, and light transforms are guided work novices can execute with a clear methodology.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused correlated-evasion measurement with an independence baseline; few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Fully external to labs with open models/detectors; weak lab incentive.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference and lightweight transforms; trivial compute.

novelty.reasoning: Detector robustness studied; correlated cross-generator evasion angle may be partially open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Detection evasion studied; cross-generator correlation angle may be open.
